item.aggregated_output:
# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Measure the bottleneck before choosing the optimization

Use the existing [timing reports](testing-feedback-loop.md#measure-feedback-before-tuning-capacity).
Distinguish time to actionable feedback, time until required checks complete,
runner execution minutes and failure/rerun frequency. A change can improve one
while worsening another. Runner minutes are not billing, and a green rerun does
not erase the first failure.

Compare equivalent source changes, test inventories, platforms, toolchains and
cache conditions. Retain cold and warm observations, sample size, cancellations
and missing data. P50/P95 from a small or mixed historical sample are descriptive;
one faster run is not a durable latency guarantee. Job creation-to-start time can
include dependencies, so do not label it all runner queue time or call the last
finishing job a proven critical path.

| Observed cost               | Investigate first                                                                 | Prefer before adding capacity                                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Waiting to start            | Actual dependency graph, runner availability, obsolete candidates, matrix fan-out | Remove unnecessary dependencies and safely cancel superseded verification            |
| Installation or compilation | Step timing, dependency graph, cache restore/save cost and compatibility          | Remove repeated setup and reuse compatible outputs; inspect Cargo timings            |
| Long test execution         | Slow cases, fixture preparation, worker saturation, shard imbalance               | Fix expensive setup and balance measured work within resource limits                 |
| Intermittent failures       | First failure logs, traces, readiness, task lifetime and leaked resources         | Reproduce and repair the owning fixture, product behavior or infrastructure          |
| Evidence collection         | Archive sizes, compression, transfer, merge and upload time                       | Produce each required report once and separate optional presentation from acceptance |

[Cargo build timings](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/timings.html)
help distinguish compilation work from test execution. A test scheduler cannot
remove compilation cost. Include dependency installation, archive transfer and
reporting in the comparison; moving cost into another job is not removing it.

Set latency and resource expectations from representative observations and the
purpose of each gate. A job timeout is a safety bound, not a performance target.
Record material budget changes and their rationale in the owning configuration
and review, rather than inventing universal minute limits in this guide.

## Reuse compatible work with verifiable inputs

Prefer one producer for an expensive output when consumers need the same inputs
and artifact transfer is cheaper than rebuilding. Include the producer dependency
and its effect on parallelism in the measurement. Reuse compilation separately
from test execution: each required consumer still supplies its own assertions.
Keep production, coverage, sanitizer and mutation configurations distinct unless
their compatibility has been established.

A cache is an optional accelerator. A cold or evicted cache must still allow
correct execution. Measure restored bytes, restore/save time, useful hits and
eviction; a reported hit alone does not prove a faster build. Preserve the
existing trust boundaries and write policy. GitHub documents cache matching,
branch access and eviction in its [dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching).

An artifact used as acceptance evidence has a stronger contract. Its consumer
must validate the actual tested head or merge source, workflow/run/attempt, platform and architecture,
relevant toolchain/features, expected inventory and content digests required by
the owning protocol. A matching filename, a successful download or a cache hit
is insufficient. Digests detect content changes; provenance establishes whether
those bytes belong to the intended candidate. Reject missing, stale, duplicate,
partial or incompatible inputs before merging evidence.

Keep these checks in the existing producer/consumer owner. Do not add a second
receipt format or evidence resolver. Exercise rejected-input cases when changing
that boundary, and preserve the documented rerun procedure for attempt-bound
artifacts. GitHub's download action reports a digest mismatch as a warning;
the evidence consumer must explicitly reject it. See [artifact validation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data#validating-artifacts)
for the platform behavior.

## Refactor coverage without losing its meaning

Two executions are redundant only when their requirement, inputs, platform and
evidence obligations are equivalent. A browser mock, real desktop process,
encrypted loopback exchange and physical network observation prove different
things. Keep the [platform evidence boundaries](platform-validation.md).

Before merging or deleting a check, map each assertion and downstream consumer
to its retained owner. Update affected selectors, fixtures, artifact consumers,
required checks and release consumers together where applicable. Validate the
replacement on the current candidate before the existing protected obligation
can be retired under the [quality gates](quality-gates.md). Eliminate redundant
aggregate jobs when direct checks provide the required enforcement; retain a
collector when it actually validates completeness or combines required evidence.

Selection and sharding need inventories, not just successful exit codes. Verify
that required cases are present, partitions are complete and disjoint where
intended, and expected platform-specific or ignored cases remain explicit.
Empty selections, skipped dependencies and incomplete collectors cannot stand in
for executed coverage. Moving Rust execution to another runner must also retain
separately owned doc-tests and integration/ignored-test obligations.

Use [same-source selection audits](testing-feedback-loop.md#qualify-affected-selection-alongside-full-gates)
before proposing narrower gates. Imports alone cannot reveal every runtime,
native or generated consumer. Moving a check from PRs to a schedule changes
detection latency and acceptance scope; describe and review that tradeoff rather
than calling it equivalent coverage delivered faster.

Workflow path filters and job conditions have different required-check behavior.
GitHub warns that a workflow skipped by path or branch filtering can leave its
required check pending; a skipped job can report success. A collector must still
run when a dependency fails and explicitly reject failed, cancelled, missing or
unexpectedly skipped required work. An `always()` condition schedules a collector;
it does not validate its dependencies. See [required-check troubleshooting](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks).

The UI HTML collector follows the mandatory full-shard producers, independently
of the optional extended-browser jobs. If Health prevents desktop shards from
starting, their missing reports remain incomplete evidence. The collector checks
all four current-attempt shards per OS; fixing the upstream failure and rerunning
the selected producers supplies that evidence, rather than omitting those OSes.

## Bound parallelism and preserve isolation

Choose shards from observed work and available runner capacity. Count setup and
artifact overhead as well as execution. More shards can increase queueing and
runner minutes; more workers per machine can increase memory pressure, port
exhaustion and test interference. Review the product of platform, architecture,
browser, feature and shard dimensions before expanding a matrix.

Retain fresh process/context isolation, owned temporary directories, dynamically
allocated ports where supported, and deterministic cleanup. Keep compile jobs,
test workers and network/rendering resource limits explicit. Do not multiply
them independently and assume the machine can absorb the combined load.
[Nextest archives](https://nexte.st/docs/ci-features/archiving/) can separate build
and execution, while [Playwright sharding](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-sharding)
distributes browser work. Archive consumers need the same source revision and
required runtime assets; shard distribution does not guarantee equal durations.
Both need compatible inputs and complete inventories, with isolation preserved.

Cancel superseded verification for the same candidate when safe, with concurrency
groups that separate caller workflows, event streams and branches. Reusable Health
keeps a distinct prefix because GitHub exposes the caller workflow in its context;
PR/merge/push candidates cancel their superseded source, while scheduled and manual
evidence streams remain isolated. Preserve
publication and release ordering. Inspect the configured queue mode and
cancellation semantics; do not assume workflow dispatch order is execution order.
Concurrency groups do not supply merge-candidate validation. Follow GitHub's
[concurrency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency)
and the project's [merge-check rules](testing-feedback-loop.md#merge-queues-and-required-merge-checks).

## Fix instability at the owning boundary

Classify a failure before changing its budget: product regression, fixture race,
resource exhaustion, dependency/service failure or unavailable infrastructure.
Retain the failing source and attempt, first error, relevant trace and measured
phase. A passing rerun is diagnostic information, not a root-cause explanation.
Playwright explicitly [classifies a retry pass as flaky](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-retries);
keep first-attempt and retry outcomes distinct.

Synchronize with observable readiness and the exact operation being tested.
Register observers before triggering transient events; correlate signals with
request identity, immutable control state and the lifetime of the actual task.
Historical logs or a previously authenticated request do not prove that a live
request has entered the required phase. Keep cancellation, task joining and
cleanup correct on success, failure and panic.

Separate expensive fixture preparation from the operation's measured window when
preparation is outside the requirement. Continue using the real signing,
persistence, transport or UI owner when it is part of the assertion. Preserve
production deadlines and real lifecycle coverage where those are the subject of
the test; changing the clock or injecting state cannot silently remove them.
The [fixture timing guidance](testing-feedback-loop.md#cold-fixture-preparation-versus-measured-progress)
owns concrete examples and permitted boundaries.

Prefer bounded condition waits and meaningful failure diagnostics. Browser
actions should use [Playwright actionability and retrying assertions](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability)
where applicable; application readiness may still need its own signal. Arbitrary
sleeps, broader timeouts, blanket retries and weaker assertions need evidence;
they are not default repairs for an unexplained failure. If a narrowly scoped
infrastructure retry is justified, keep its limit, original failure and outcomes
visible, and ensure repeating the operation is safe. Test retries still obey the
owning suite policy.

For a reproducible race or timeout fix, use a regression or negative control that
fails for the original mechanism and passes with the repair. Confirm that the
intended case actually ran. Preserve existing coverage while investigating; any
temporary quarantine needs an explicit owner, reason, tracking issue and removal
condition under the existing gate policy.

## Reject incomplete discovery and generated-policy drift

Successful test execution requires successful, complete input discovery.
`scripts/ci/fuzz-targets.py` compares the discovered cargo-fuzz list with the actual
manifest-owned target inventory before running anything. Failed enumeration, an
empty list, duplicates, omissions or unknown targets fail the job, as do individual
target failures. Keep this assertion at the execution owner; shell loop command
substitution alone does not propagate discovery failure under `set -e`.

`scripts/ci/glib-migration.py` evaluates every resolved glib branch, rather than
treating a newer parallel branch as proof that an older stack was removed. Its
migration claim conservatively requires stable 0.20 or newer throughout; absent
glib and mixed old/new trees do not establish migration. The
[RustSec advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html) owns the
security version ranges; the watcher retains native build/test and reviewed-PR
requirements before changing dependencies.

Generated native input probes share one accepted-key/extended-flag metadata owner
between WebDriver mapping and emitted C# policy. Regressions must check that every
emitted key is accepted with the correct flags and unsupported keys remain
rejected, rather than only matching the generated call text. Ownership checks and
real desktop acceptance remain separate from generator/compilation checks.

## Review the change and prevent renewed drift

Follow the existing validation stages; do not invent a parallel completion
process. For changes affecting CI behavior or recurring cost, include the
following in the normal [alignment review](maintenance-checklist.md#review-and-follow-up-procedure):

- The acceptance boundary and retained owner, including consumers affected by
  deletion, merging, selection or schedule changes.
- The measured bottleneck, comparable before/after scope and remaining unknowns;
  distinguish observed latency, resource cost and reliability.
- Executed validation and source identity, with inventory/provenance checks or
  regression controls appropriate to the changed mechanism.
- Remaining hosted, cross-platform, native or release evidence and the owner of
  any follow-up. Do not claim candidate acceptance from local or older results.

Workflow, runner and tool upgrades can change CLI semantics, report formats,
selectors and archive compatibility. Validate affected real tool invocations and
failure paths through the existing diagnostic owners; YAML parsing or unit mocks
alone do not establish the behavior of the installed tool.

Revisit timing and failure evidence when a gate becomes slower, starts rerunning,
gains another platform/dependency, or repeatedly exceeds its expected budget.
During existing maintenance reviews, inspect slow cases, duplicated setup,
shard imbalance, cache churn and abandoned temporary exceptions. Retire obsolete
work with its consumers and selectors rather than accumulating permanent layers.

Keep this review proportional: a documentation-only change needs applicable
formatting, links and structural checks, not a new build benchmark. Rules should
be enforceable through existing contracts and diagnostics where practical;
adding this guide does not create a scheduled job or another required check.
# AI coding reliability guide

Use this guide before implementing or reviewing a change, especially a bug fix,
refactor, merge resolution or optimization. Its purpose is to turn recurring
failure modes into concrete design questions and executable checks. Compiling,
adding a timeout or passing a happy-path test does not establish reliability.

This guide owns the cross-cutting review method and reusable failure patterns.
[Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) owns implementation boundaries;
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [network contracts](network-design-reference.md)
and feature guides own behavior and resource limits. The
[testing workflow](testing-feedback-loop.md) owns commands, selection and gates.
Link to those owners instead of copying their changing contracts here. When code
and a contract disagree, resolve the intended behavior rather than documenting
the regression as the new rule.

## Use on every change

1. **Locate the owner and consumers.** Read the owning implementation, callers,
   existing tests and relevant guide before adding another helper or state owner.
   Include callbacks, IPC handlers, retries, startup, shutdown and recovery paths;
   an import graph alone cannot reveal all consumers.
2. **State the invariant and select risks.** Describe what must remain true on
   success, failure, cancellation and replacement. Use the table below to select
   applicable rules. A small diff can change lock order or lifetime semantics.
3. **Trace the failure path before editing.** For concurrency work, sketch who
   owns each lock, permit, task and mutable state; what it waits for; and who
   releases it. For a reproducible bug, construct a focused failing regression.
   Record unresolved hypotheses as hypotheses, not confirmed defects.
4. **Implement at the existing boundary.** Preserve authority, durable acceptance,
   compatibility and resource budgets. Recheck invariants after moving work
   outside a guard. Evaluate the proposed fix for new races and deadlocks too.
5. **Verify the changed boundary and report evidence.** Run affected checks and
   required boundary scenarios under the testing workflow. Explain results,
   exclusions and unresolved evidence. Update this guide when the defect exposes
   a reusable failure pattern; follow the maintenance procedure below.

Keep the risk explanation proportional to the change. A documentation edit does
not require a new concurrency test. A changed async callback does require a
lifetime review even when the diff is one line. Put task-specific reasoning and
results in the PR or ignored local evidence, not a new permanent report.

## Select rules by the changed boundary

| Change or symptom                                                        | Read at least                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Locks, callbacks, synchronous dispatch, UI freezes                       | [R01](#r01-lock-order-and-reentrant-calls), [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure)                |
| Background work, native providers, logout, shutdown or cancellation      | [R02](#r02-thread-and-scheduler-progress), [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions)               |
| Network requests, retries, polling, queues or batches                    | [R03](#r03-actual-work-owns-its-lifetime), [R04](#r04-deadlines-cover-the-whole-operation), [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)          |
| React effects, IPC reads, dialogs, optimistic updates or mutation status | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R07](#r07-observation-is-not-mutation-ownership), [R10](#r10-evidence-that-exercises-the-failure) |
| Storage, settings, imports, deletion or recovery                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| IPC/API inputs, files, media or protocol changes                         | [R06](#r06-exact-authority-and-stale-completions), [R08](#r08-durable-state-and-failure-semantics), [R09](#r09-bound-input-and-resource-use)          |
| Merge resolution, shared helper or dependency changes                    | Revisit the affected callers and all applicable rules; a clean textual merge does not establish compatible ownership or semantics.                    |

These are starting points, not permission to ignore another reachable boundary.
Do not add a global lock, retry loop, timeout or shared abstraction solely to make
the local symptom disappear.

A frozen UI may result from a lock cycle, blocked event thread, starvation, lost
wakeup, unbounded work or stale loading state. Identify the mechanism and the
missing progress condition before selecting a fix; these need different evidence.

## R01: Lock order and reentrant calls

**Failure pattern:** one path takes A then B while another takes B then A; or a
helper/callback reacquires a nonrecursive lock its caller already holds. The
second case can deadlock on a single thread. Nested reads also need review when
a queued writer can prevent a new read from completing.

Trace actual acquisition order through callees, authorization callbacks,
destructors and error cleanup. Include main-thread dispatch and task joins as
wait dependencies, not just mutexes. A typical UI cycle is:

```text
background task: holds session guard -> waits for main-thread callback
main thread:     handles UI event    -> waits for session guard
```

Use the owning module's order; do not invent one universal order for unrelated
subsystems. Make whether a helper acquires a guard or requires one explicit.
Avoid invoking arbitrary callbacks while guarded. Where a commit callback must
run inside an authority guard, keep that contract narrow and inspect its complete
call chain. Queue presentation without retaining a guard needed by the UI;
validate captured authority when the queued callback executes.

**Evidence:** exercise both competing paths and the real authorization variant.
An ordinary admission fixture does not cover a sensitive proof that itself locks
app state. Assert that the other operation progresses, not just that the first
eventually returns. See `checked_at_lock_revision` in
[runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs), the verified-login
regression in [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs),
and queued notification tests in [runtime state](../src-tauri/src/chat_commands/state.rs).

## R02: Thread and scheduler progress

**Failure pattern:** an `async` function performs blocking disk, crypto, OS-provider
or process work; a blocking worker retains a globally needed guard; or the parent
scheduler awaits optional work before polling unrelated ready operations.

Identify the executing thread and scheduling owner, not just the function's
signature. Move blocking work through the existing admitted worker boundary.
Inspect React render/effect/subscriber feedback loops and large synchronous data
transforms too; moving I/O off the UI thread does not bound those CPU costs.
Prepare bulk data outside shared commit guards, then reacquire the required
guards and revalidate before atomic publication. Keep critical sections small
without splitting a transaction or permitting stale side effects. Replacing a
mutex with an async mutex alone does not repair ownership or lock order.

Check that the UI event loop, accept loop and control scheduler can still make
progress while the worker is paused. Offloading a scan does not help other
branches of a scheduler if that scheduler still waits for the entire scan inside
one completion branch. Synchronous final persistence can still block; document
that boundary instead of claiming a timer can preempt it.

**Evidence:** pause actual expensive work after admission and assert availability
of the unrelated guard or operation. Release the pause and verify the final data.
See the attachment preparation and document-scheduler regressions in
[account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs).

## R03: Actual work owns its lifetime

**Failure pattern:** cancelling an awaiter releases serialization or capacity while
its blocking worker, process or native provider continues; retries overlap, old
work writes into a new session, or shutdown waits for a worker while holding a
guard that worker needs to finish.

Name the owner of every task, timer, listener, subprocess, socket and permit.
Transfer required ownership into the actual work. Dropping an observer or timing
out a future is not evidence that external side effects stopped. Retain mutation
serialization and cleanup responsibility until real completion; bound admission
so repeated user retries cannot accumulate detached work.

Follow the existing retirement protocol: close admission, signal cancellation,
release guards needed for completion, join owned tasks and drain admitted work.
Uncancellable native work needs an explicit ownership boundary: retain the
operation's serialization ownership, but not unrelated runtime/session guards across
the provider call. Revalidate publication and compensate stale effects through
the owner. A timeout is not permission to abandon durable work or reuse its slot.

**Evidence:** cancel the caller while work is paused; confirm retirement progress
where promised, retained serialization, eventual cleanup and absence of stale
publication. Include repeated cancellation and a successful noncancelled case.
See [shared login tests](../src-tauri/src/shared_account_login/tests.rs) and the
runtime lifecycle boundaries in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

## R04: Deadlines cover the whole operation

**Failure pattern:** each route or phase has a timeout, but queueing, admission,
serial alternatives or retries make the complete user operation effectively
unbounded. A generic timeout error also triggers the wrong retry/recovery path.

Use the existing owning budget for the whole logical operation, including permit
waits and all alternatives; carry its remaining time into subordinate work where
needed. Distinguish observation deadlines, admission refusal and transport failure.
Preserve the owner-defined retry policy and original operation identity. Do not
reset the overall budget on every attempt or increase it just to hide a hang.

Check cancellation cleanup and late completion as well as elapsed time. Async
timers cannot interrupt a thread blocked in a synchronous mutex, native call or
filesystem syscall. Such a path also needs R01–R03. Budget values remain in the
[network contracts](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and implementation, rather than a second set of constants here.

**Evidence:** stall admission and a later network phase separately, use multiple
candidate routes, and verify permits/socket owners are released. Check that an
expired preflight has no partial durable mutation. Examples live in
[privacy runtime tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_runtime_tests.rs)
and [group invitation tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/tests.rs).

## R05: Bounded work must also make progress

**Failure pattern:** taking the first N entries every turn permanently excludes
older pending work; failed items pin a cursor; unbounded retries flood a queue;
or a completion signal arrives between checking a condition and registering a
waiter, leaving work asleep indefinitely.

Review fairness across successive turns, not only the batch size. Use the existing
cursor, coalescing and admission owners; distinguish independent lanes where
needed. Failed publication must not indefinitely prevent later eligible work.
Recheck conditions with the synchronization primitive's correct waiter protocol;
a notification alone is not the durable condition. Preserve startup, wake,
shutdown and missed-notification recovery behavior.

Keep independent reasons for continuing work separate. A worker can finish a
history page and then fail an optional favorites exchange; reporting that error
must not discard unfinished history or a refresh received during the exchange.
Consume a coalesced wake only when its follow-up remains scheduled after every
error branch. A failure without pending work must still avoid a busy retry loop.

Retain demand throughout backoff. A future retry deadline makes queued work
temporarily ineligible; it does not consume that work. Wake the existing scheduler
at the earliest retained deadline when a worker is available, without relying on
periodic repair. A queued deadline must not spin while its worker is occupied.
The `account_history_capacity_backoff_retains_demand_without_periodic_repair`
regression in [account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
checks real admission contention, retained work and the unchanged backoff.

Keep count, byte, task and concurrency budgets intact. Fair scheduling does not
guarantee a successful write into a full store, justify eviction of durable intent
or permit increasing capacity without reviewing consumers.

Finite preparation must survive unrelated ordinary appends without relaxing its
authority fences. Compare the owner's complete control and destructive revisions;
an unfinished derived index cannot certify a concurrent append. Capture completed
index readiness so later turns can progress. The ordinary-append and pending
observation regressions in [participant network selection](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/privacy_sync/network.rs)
exercise progress alongside capability, proof, roster and file-policy invalidation.

**Evidence:** create more eligible items than one batch, put pending work behind
terminal history, and include a failed item, cancellation and newly arriving work.
Assert progress and budget preservation across turns. See publication rotation
tests in the [group journal](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_group/operations/journal.rs).
The `account_history_after_favorites_*` regressions in
[account sync tests](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/account_sync/selection_tests.rs)
cover successful and failed optional exchanges, retained refreshes, unfinished
history pages and failure without pending work.

## R06: Exact authority and stale completions

**Failure pattern:** work authorized before an await or queue delay commits after
logout, same-user relogin, account replacement or a policy off/on transition.
Comparing only the username or current Boolean value misses changed authority.

Capture the owner's exact session/runtime installation and relevant revision at
entry. Revalidate through the existing atomic commit seam before side effects
and before publishing private results. Treat frontend generation guards as UI
ownership, not host authorization. Read commands can expose stale private data too.

Account for reentrant store subscribers and callbacks that can retire an owner
synchronously during publication. Lock once when combining sensitive proof and
revision checks. If a guard must be released around preparation, reacquire it and
check all invalidating conditions; an earlier successful check is insufficient.
Compensation must identify the stale operation's own effects and must not erase
newer valid state.

them, too. A component-wide decode failure can suppress a replacement image,
and a retired load callback can publish stale geometry. The
[inline media owner](module-boundaries.md#inline-media-presentation) binds both
outcomes to the current URL and session; the replacement-source and retired-load
regressions in [MediaPreview tests](../frontend/src/features/chat/MediaPreview.test.ts)
exercise recovery and rejection of stale callbacks.

owner, change the relevant policy revision, or remove the source; then resume.

The [desktop session owner](module-boundaries.md#2-feature-owners-and-shared-decisions)
and [runtime admission](../src-tauri/src/runtime_admission.rs) define the shared seam.

## R07: Observation is not mutation ownership

**Failure pattern:** a never-settling read leaves the UI busy forever; a timeout
is treated as failed durable mutation; clearing a busy flag allows duplicate
submission while the original native write continues; optional hydration hides
a known successful commit.

offer a recoverable UI state. Preserve the actual mutation's ownership, ordering
and exact operation ID until its real outcome is known. Unknown admission must
remain unknown; reconcile or retry according to the owning idempotency contract.
Process a late definite refusal without fabricating a protocol terminal state.
Do not turn failed readback into an empty successful save or resend an accepted
message because optional roster, preview or notification work failed.

duplicate action, then settle the original call with success and with refusal in
separate cases. Switch sessions during the wait. Assert bounded UI observation,
no overlapping mutation and correct late settlement. See
[group operation tests](../frontend/src/store/accountGroupOperations.test.ts),
[outgoing intent tests](../frontend/src/store/outgoingIntent.test.ts) and
[coordinated state owners](module-boundaries.md#coordinated-state-owners).

## R08: Durable state and failure semantics

**Failure pattern:** a read-modify-write race loses another update; optimistic
success precedes durable acceptance; retries duplicate writes; a failed/corrupt
read is silently treated as empty state; cleanup after a partial failure destroys
recoverable user data.

Prepare expensive work separately, then compare expected revision and lifetime
under the owning commit guard. Preserve operation IDs, ordering, atomic replacement
and existing compatibility rules. Multi-store changes are not automatically one
transaction; define recovery or compensation for every partial commit boundary.
Use established error types and distinguish absent, unavailable and corrupt data.

Preserve accepted intent when presentation fails. Report what actually committed;
do not relabel a committed change as rejected because later best-effort work
failed. Avoid empty catches, blanket defaults or unconditional retries that hide
the distinction. Follow the owning feature guide for rollback and durability.

**Evidence:** fail before and after the commit point, interleave a second writer,
retry with the same identity, and restart using retained data. Verify acknowledged
state survives, stale cleanup cannot delete a newer write, and partial outcomes
are reported honestly. See [development conventions](../specifications/development_conventions.md)
and the feature-specific owners in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

**Failure pattern:** peer/UI-controlled data expands into unbounded allocation,
recursive traversal, decode work, fanout or task creation; a file path crosses its
allowed namespace; a convenient new IPC endpoint bypasses the existing admission
or authorization owner.

existing frame, file, count, depth and byte limits. Preserve exact account/device
bindings and path/consent checks. Display metadata and frontend validation are
not authorization. Bound queues and retained retry state as well as active work;
do not remove backpressure to make a benchmark look faster.

**Evidence:** test the limit and just beyond it, malformed or missing data,
wrong-owner requests, saturation and recovery after capacity returns. Include
real loopback assertions for changed networking/crypto boundaries as required by
the [network review matrix](network-design-reference.md#minimum-feature-review-matrix).
Keep secrets and private payloads out of diagnostic logs and fixtures.

## R10: Evidence that exercises the failure

Use barriers, deferred promises, injected provider/storage stalls and controlled
clocks at the actual boundary. Prefer an observable progress assertion to an
arbitrary sleep or a test that checks only that a timeout helper was called.
Verify successful behavior, failure, cleanup and replacement through the same
production owner; a mock that bypasses the problematic lock proves little.

Give connection setup and capability negotiation their own bounded watchdog.
Start a progress deadline only after the required stalled operation is admitted,
and prove the competing work is still incomplete at that point. Release only
that work's barrier while retaining the stall. Measure cancellation separately
from setup and history progress; preserve each behavior's required bound.

A periodic probe can miss readiness between its last check and the deadline.
Use [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)'s waiter protocol to recheck
the actual condition on a transition, retaining the original deadline and bounded
fallback. A snapshot taken after timeout is diagnostic evidence, not success.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or
the absence of every deadlock. Cancelled, interrupted, empty and unavailable runs
remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.

## Review record

For applicable risks, make these answers reviewable in the PR or task result:

- **Owner and invariant:** which implementation and authoritative rule apply?
- **Risks:** which rule IDs apply, and what reachable failure path was checked?
- **Progress and lifetime:** what can wait, what stays available, and who owns work
  after cancellation, retirement or retry?
- **Commit and authority:** what becomes durable, what invalidates permission,
  and how are stale or partially completed effects handled?
- **Evidence:** which regression/scenario exercised the boundary on which source,
  and what actually passed, failed or remained unverified?

Use concrete paths, operations and assertions. “Thread safe,” “handles errors,”
“tests pass” and checked boxes without evidence are not sufficient explanations.
For a nonapplicable risk, a short reason is enough; do not manufacture tests or
ceremonial reports for unrelated concerns.

## Keep the guide useful as defects are found

The author of a confirmed defect fix owns the corresponding guidance update;
the reviewer checks it alongside the regression and owning contract. Follow the
[requirement maintenance loop](testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

1. Identify the missing general decision, not just the incident's file or symptom.
   Strengthen an existing rule when it already covers the mechanism.
2. Add a new stable rule ID only for a distinct, reusable failure pattern. Include
   **trigger, failure mechanism, required approach, authoritative owner and
   observable regression evidence**. Add its route to the selection table.
3. Update the owning implementation/guide and affected `validation.json` selectors,
   consumers or scenarios when needed. A prose reminder cannot replace the test
   or make an unselected regression part of future checks.
4. Maintain example links when code moves; update rule references when rules merge
   or retire. Do not silently reuse an ID for a different meaning. Remove obsolete
   advice rather than appending conflicting exceptions or dated status updates.

commit diaries, machine-specific commands or a parallel copy of feature contracts.
Unconfirmed suspicions belong in an issue or ignored investigation notes. This
guide supports engineering judgment and executable validation; it cannot make
unreviewed generated code reliable by itself.

# Keeping CI fast and reliable

Treat feedback time, reliability and resource use as maintained requirements.
Every feature, dependency and test can change CI cost, even without a workflow
edit. AI agents and contributors should preserve useful coverage while reducing
unnecessary work, and leave failures easier to reproduce and diagnose.

This guide owns CI maintenance decisions and regression prevention. It does not
introduce another workflow, command catalog or acceptance policy.

| Question                                            | Authoritative owner                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Which tests, commands and CI jobs apply?            | [Testing feedback loop](testing-feedback-loop.md), owning `validation.json` contracts and [workflow definitions](../.github/workflows/) |
| What evidence permits acceptance or release?        | [Quality gates](quality-gates.md) and [version and release lifecycle](updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)                       |
| Where does an implementation or shared rule belong? | [Module ownership](module-boundaries.md) and [script entry points](../scripts/README.md)                                                |
| Which consumers and documentation need updating?    | [Change alignment checklist](maintenance-checklist.md) and [documentation guidelines](DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md)                      |

Keep tool versions, matrix sizes, deadlines, cache keys and required-check names
in their existing executable owners. Keep run histories and investigation output
in ignored `tmp/` or PR/CI artifacts; durable decisions belong in the owning guide.

## Make the cost of a change explicit

Before adding a suite, fixture, dependency, platform or workflow, identify the
existing owner and the observable failure it must detect. Inspect the affected
plan and consumers through the [validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities).
Answer four questions in the change when they are material:

- What requirement needs new evidence, and why is existing evidence insufficient?
- Which layer and platform can exercise that requirement faithfully?
- What recurring setup, compilation, execution and artifact cost will it add?
- Can an existing task, fixture or compatible output supply it without weakening
  assertions or introducing another owner for the same rule?

Extend the existing implementation first. Share policy and lifecycle rules where
their meaning is identical; keep feature-specific fixtures local. An abstraction
is useful when it removes duplicated decisions and has clear inputs, outputs and
failure behavior. Avoid both copied shell fragments and a generic CI framework
whose configuration is harder to review than the work it coordinates.

Do not make a full local suite the default for every edit. Use affected feedback
while developing, then complete the applicable boundary and candidate gates.
New tests still need independent assertions; matching the implementation or
increasing a test count does not establish useful coverage.

## Measure the bottleneck before choosing the optimization

Use the existing [timing reports](testing-feedback-loop.md#measure-feedback-before-tuning-capacity).
Distinguish time to actionable feedback, time until required checks complete,
runner execution minutes and failure/rerun frequency. A change can improve one
while worsening another. Runner minutes are not billing, and a green rerun does
not erase the first failure.

cache conditions. Retain cold and warm observations, sample size, cancellations
and missing data. P50/P95 from a small or mixed historical sample are descriptive;
one faster run is not a durable latency guarantee. Job creation-to-start time can
include dependencies, so do not label it all runner queue time or call the last
finishing job a proven critical path.

| Observed cost               | Investigate first                                                                 | Prefer before adding capacity                                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Waiting to start            | Actual dependency graph, runner availability, obsolete candidates, matrix fan-out | Remove unnecessary dependencies and safely cancel superseded verification            |
| Installation or compilation | Step timing, dependency graph, cache restore/save cost and compatibility          | Remove repeated setup and reuse compatible outputs; inspect Cargo timings            |
| Long test execution         | Slow cases, fixture preparation, worker saturation, shard imbalance               | Fix expensive setup and balance measured work within resource limits                 |
| Intermittent failures       | First failure logs, traces, readiness, task lifetime and leaked resources         | Reproduce and repair the owning fixture, product behavior or infrastructure          |
| Evidence collection         | Archive sizes, compression, transfer, merge and upload time                       | Produce each required report once and separate optional presentation from acceptance |

[Cargo build timings](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/timings.html)

remove compilation cost. Include dependency installation, archive transfer and
reporting in the comparison; moving cost into another job is not removing it.

purpose of each gate. A job timeout is a safety bound, not a performance target.

## Reuse compatible work with verifiable inputs

Prefer one producer for an expensive output when consumers need the same inputs
and artifact transfer is cheaper than rebuilding. Include the producer dependency
and its effect on parallelism in the measurement. Reuse compilation separately
from test execution: each required consumer still supplies its own assertions.

their compatibility has been established.

correct execution. Measure restored bytes, restore/save time, useful hits and
eviction; a reported hit alone does not prove a faster build. Preserve the

## R08: Durable state and failure semantics

**Failure pattern:** a read-modify-write race loses another update; optimistic
success precedes durable acceptance; retries duplicate writes; a failed/corrupt
read is silently treated as empty state; cleanup after a partial failure destroys
recoverable user data.

Identify the commit point, serialization owner and restart/replay behavior.
Prepare expensive work separately, then compare expected revision and lifetime
under the owning commit guard. Preserve operation IDs, ordering, atomic replacement
and existing compatibility rules. Multi-store changes are not automatically one
transaction; define recovery or compensation for every partial commit boundary.
Use established error types and distinguish absent, unavailable and corrupt data.

Preserve accepted intent when presentation fails. Report what actually committed;
do not relabel a committed change as rejected because later best-effort work
failed. Avoid empty catches, blanket defaults or unconditional retries that hide
the distinction. Follow the owning feature guide for rollback and durability.

**Evidence:** fail before and after the commit point, interleave a second writer,
retry with the same identity, and restart using retained data. Verify acknowledged
state survives, stale cleanup cannot delete a newer write, and partial outcomes
are reported honestly. See [development conventions](../specifications/development_conventions.md)
and the feature-specific owners in [module ownership](module-boundaries.md).

## R09: Bound input and resource use

**Failure pattern:** peer/UI-controlled data expands into unbounded allocation,
recursive traversal, decode work, fanout or task creation; a file path crosses its
allowed namespace; a convenient new IPC endpoint bypasses the existing admission
or authorization owner.

Validate at the owning trust boundary before allocation and side effects, using
existing frame, file, count, depth and byte limits. Preserve exact account/device
bindings and path/consent checks. Display metadata and frontend validation are
not authorization. Bound queues and retained retry state as well as active work;
do not remove backpressure to make a benchmark look faster.

**Evidence:** test the limit and just beyond it, malformed or missing data,
wrong-owner requests, saturation and recovery after capacity returns. Include
real loopback assertions for changed networking/crypto boundaries as required by
the [network review matrix](network-design-reference.md#minimum-feature-review-matrix).
Keep secrets and private payloads out of diagnostic logs and fixtures.

## R10: Evidence that exercises the failure

Use barriers, deferred promises, injected provider/storage stalls and controlled
clocks at the actual boundary. Prefer an observable progress assertion to an
arbitrary sleep or a test that checks only that a timeout helper was called.
Verify successful behavior, failure, cleanup and replacement through the same
production owner; a mock that bypasses the problematic lock proves little.

Give connection setup and capability negotiation their own bounded watchdog.
Start a progress deadline only after the required stalled operation is admitted,
and prove the competing work is still incomplete at that point. Release only
that work's barrier while retaining the stall. Measure cancellation separately
from setup and history progress; preserve each behavior's required bound.

A periodic probe can miss readiness between its last check and the deadline.
Use [R05](#r05-bounded-work-must-also-make-progress)'s waiter protocol to recheck
the actual condition on a transition, retaining the original deadline and bounded
fallback. A snapshot taken after timeout is diagnostic evidence, not success.

A deadlock regression must not hang its own runner: bound coordination, arrange
fixture release even when assertions fail, and use an isolated process with an
outer deadline when a synchronous lock cycle cannot be safely unwound. An async
timeout inside the blocked thread is not sufficient. Avoid port-selection races
and process-global fixtures that assume serial execution; respect the repository's
test environment and resource controls.

Treat a lock-order suspicion, a reproduced bug and a passing regression as
different evidence. A stack sample or total suite duration alone does not prove
one test is deadlocked. Inspect the active operation, its duration and the actual
wait dependencies. Preserve required assertions when fixing flaky setup; do not
hide a failure with retries, larger sleeps, skipped tests or weaker selectors.

Record the tested source, command, environment, count and outcome. Reassess
consumers after merging new callers or changing a shared helper. Static scans,
passing unit tests and browser IPC mocks do not establish native OS behavior or
the absence of every deadlock. Cancelled, interrupted, empty and unavailable runs
remain distinct from passes. Completed individual commands do not turn a cancelled
parent run into a passing full gate. Follow the
[validation protocol](testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
and keep unresolved native, cross-platform and stress obligations explicit.

## Review record

For applicable risks, make these answers reviewable in the PR or task result:

- **Owner and invariant:** which implementation and authoritative rule apply?
- **Risks:** which rule IDs apply, and what reachable failure path was checked?
- **Progress and lifetime:** what can wait, what stays available, and who owns work
  after cancellation, retirement or retry?
- **Commit and authority:** what becomes durable, what invalidates permission,
  and how are stale or partially completed effects handled?
- **Evidence:** which regression/scenario exercised the boundary on which source,
  and what actually passed, failed or remained unverified?

Use concrete paths, operations and assertions. “Thread safe,” “handles errors,”
“tests pass” and checked boxes without evidence are not sufficient explanations.
For a nonapplicable risk, a short reason is enough; do not manufacture tests or
ceremonial reports for unrelated concerns.

## Keep the guide useful as defects are found

The author of a confirmed defect fix owns the corresponding guidance update;
the reviewer checks it alongside the regression and owning contract. Follow the
[requirement maintenance loop](testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

1. Identify the missing general decision, not just the incident's file or symptom.
   Strengthen an existing rule when it already covers the mechanism.
2. Add a new stable rule ID only for a distinct, reusable failure pattern. Include
   **trigger, failure mechanism, required approach, authoritative owner and
   observable regression evidence**. Add its route to the selection table.
3. Update the owning implementation/guide and affected `validation.json` selectors,
   consumers or scenarios when needed. A prose reminder cannot replace the test
   or make an unselected regression part of future checks.
4. Maintain example links when code moves; update rule references when rules merge
   or retire. Do not silently reuse an ID for a different meaning. Remove obsolete
   advice rather than appending conflicting exceptions or dated status updates.

Keep this a compact set of reusable decisions. Do not add test-count histories,
commit diaries, machine-specific commands or a parallel copy of feature contracts.
Unconfirmed suspicions belong in an issue or ignored investigation notes. This
guide supports engineering judgment and executable validation; it cannot make
unreviewed generated code reliable by itself.
"}

name: CI

on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Preserve the former weekly full-health Rust run.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      diagnostic_timing:
        description: Full-workspace test-only delivery phase timings
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'push' }}

# Read-only: every job just checks out and runs tooling — nothing writes back.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep stack file/line diagnostics without generating type/variable debug data.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing && '1' || '0' }}

jobs:
  checks:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Windows uses the reusable single-build archive workflow below. Linux
      # and macOS retain their complete linked workspace and coverage passes.
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs

      # Tauri v2 system libraries (Linux only).
      - name: Install Tauri system dependencies (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Cache Rust build
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          workspaces: . -> target
          key: workspace-checks
          cache-on-failure: true

      - name: Install frontend dependencies and check standards
        shell: bash
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix frontend
          node scripts/validation/standards.mjs
          node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov and cargo-nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov@0.8.7,cargo-nextest@0.9.148

      - name: Verify coverage accumulation with the actual tool
        run: node --test scripts/ci/backend-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/native-host-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/rust-profile.test.mjs

      # Tauri reads frontendDist, so build the frontend before any Cargo step.
      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run check:build-syntax

      # Keep native lint, production builds and instrumented tests on every OS.
      - name: Clippy
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

      # Collect each OS's workspace coverage without repeating its test suite.
      # Every platform collects coverage in its existing test pass: native-only
      # updater policy cannot be represented by Linux's AppImage-only branch.
      # --workspace covers the protocol, integrations, MCP adapter and desktop app.
      - name: Test + coverage (macOS)
        if: matrix.os != 'ubuntu-latest'
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        env:
          RUST_TEST_THREADS: 4
          NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS: 4
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          run_coverage() {
            cargo llvm-cov nextest --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk --no-tests fail --no-fail-fast --retries 0 --user-config-file none --profile default --success-output immediate
            # Preserve each failure even if another test prevents suite completion.
            cargo llvm-cov --no-report --locked --workspace --exclude mesh-talk -- --nocapture
            cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path lcov.info
          }
          if [ "$MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING" = 1 ]; then
            run_coverage 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/mesh-talk-test-timing.log"
          else
            run_coverage
          fi
          # llvm-cov runs unit/integration tests; stable Rust doctests keep their
          # original separate check without executing those suites twice.
          cargo test --workspace --doc

      - name: Test + coverage (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          run_coverage() {
            cargo llvm-cov nextest --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk --no-tests fail --no-fail-fast --retries 0 --user-config-file none --profile default --success-output immediate
            # Preserve each failure even if another test prevents suite completion.
            cargo llvm-cov --no-report --locked --workspace --exclude mesh-talk -- --nocapture
            cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path lcov.info
          }
          if [ "$MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING" = 1 ]; then
            run_coverage 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/mesh-talk-test-timing.log"
          else
            run_coverage
          fi

      - name: Workspace doctests (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: cargo test --workspace --doc --locked

      - name: Multi-process core evidence and coverage (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        shell: bash
        env:
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results
          EVAL_COVERAGE: '1'
        run: |
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs
          cargo llvm-cov --no-report -p mesh-talk-core --test bridge_cross_lan -- --ignored --test-threads=1

      - name: Large-folder enqueue regression (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          large_folder_status=0
          cargo llvm-cov test --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk-core --test large_directory_enqueue large_directory_enqueue_uses_compact_manifest_instead_of_frame_error -- --exact --ignored --test-threads=1 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log" || large_folder_status=$?
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" >&2
          if (( large_folder_status != 0 )); then exit "$large_folder_status"; fi
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --validate-large-folder "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log"
          cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path src-tauri/e2e-lcov.info

      - name: Preserve Linux backend evaluation evidence
        if: always() && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: backend-core-ubuntu-24.04-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Upload test timing diagnostics
        if: always() && env.MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING == '1'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-timing-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/mesh-talk-test-timing.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        # Dependabot PRs to dev cannot read the Actions CODECOV_TOKEN secret.
        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        if: >-
          !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
            github.base_ref == 'dev' &&
            github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && 'src-tauri/lcov.info,src-tauri/e2e-lcov.info' || 'src-tauri/lcov.info' }}
          name: workspace-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Branch protection requires codecov/patch; surface upload failures in CI too.
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  windows:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/windows-workspace.yml
    with:
      diagnostic_timing: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing || false }}
    secrets: inherit
name: Code Quality and Health Check

# Portable checks run independently of native builds and browsers. CI owns Rust
# workspace compilation/unit tests; UI E2E owns full Chromium on all platforms.
# scripts/check-health.sh remains the standalone comprehensive local gate.
on:
  workflow_call:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: health-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'push' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  platform:
    name: Portable checks (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-26-intel, windows-latest]
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Install pinned native inspection toolchain
        run: python scripts/release/sevenzip.py install
      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci
      - name: Frontend static checks
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm run format:check
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
      - name: Audit frontend dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npx --yes audit-ci --config audit-ci.json

      - name: Validate public help and MCP
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix tools/help --ignore-scripts
          node --test tools/help/*.test.mjs

      - name: Audit help dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm audit --prefix tools/help --audit-level=high

      - name: Frontend unit tests and coverage
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Frontend unit tests (macOS and Windows)
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm test

      - name: Seal browser unit line map from this run
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: node scripts/ci/unit-coverage-artifact.mjs seal frontend/coverage/lcov.info target/ui-unit-coverage

      - name: Upload browser unit line map
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ui-unit-coverage-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: target/ui-unit-coverage/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload frontend coverage
        if: always() && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: frontend-coverage-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: frontend/coverage/
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Delivery and AI eval smoke
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          make eval-smoke
          node --test scripts/test-ai-eval.mjs

      - name: Install Rust for diagnostic Cargo fixtures
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Native release inspection regression
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y nsis

      - name: Verify native NSIS payload equivalence
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: python scripts/release/test_native_nsis.py -v

      - name: Diagnostic and release gate regressions (all platforms)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs
          node --test scripts/diagnostics/*.test.mjs

      - name: Build retention safeguards (all platforms)
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_build_retention.py -v

      - name: Publish frontend coverage
        if: >-
          matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' &&
          !(github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
            github.base_ref == 'dev' &&
            github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: frontend/coverage/lcov.info
          name: frontend-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  source:
    name: Source and supply-chain checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      # Source/policy scanners have identical inputs on each OS; run them once.
      # Gitleaks owns the full-history secret scan in its independent workflow.
      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - name: Rust formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Install source scanners
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny,cargo-machete,typos-cli,shellcheck
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: '1.25'
          cache: false
      - name: Install workflow scanner
        run: |
          go install github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Source and supply-chain policy
        run: |
          typos
          cargo deny check
          cargo machete
          shellcheck --severity=warning scripts/*.sh scripts/release/*.sh .claude/hooks/*.sh hooks/*
          actionlint

        if: runner.os == 'Linux'

        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'

            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf

          components: clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Cache Rust build

        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1

        run: node --test scripts/ci/backend-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/native-host-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/rust-profile.test.mjs

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: frontend

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView

      - name: Clippy
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace
        working-directory: src-tauri

      # Every platform collects coverage in its existing test pass: native-only
      # updater policy cannot be represented by Linux's AppImage-only branch.

      - name: Test + coverage (macOS)

            # Preserve each failure even if another test prevents suite completion.
            cargo llvm-cov --no-report --locked --workspace --exclude mesh-talk -- --nocapture

      - name: Test + coverage (Linux)

        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          run_coverage() {

            # Preserve each failure even if another test prevents suite completion.

      - name: Workspace doctests (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'

      - name: Large-folder enqueue regression (Linux)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          large_folder_status=0
          cargo llvm-cov test --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk-core --test large_directory_enqueue large_directory_enqueue_uses_compact_manifest_instead_of_frame_error -- --exact --ignored --test-threads=1 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log" || large_folder_status=$?
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" >&2
          if (( large_folder_status != 0 )); then exit "$large_folder_status"; fi
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --validate-large-folder "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log"
          cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path src-tauri/e2e-lcov.info

# Portable checks run independently of native builds and browsers. CI owns Rust
# workspace compilation/unit tests; UI E2E owns full Chromium on all platforms.
# scripts/check-health.sh remains the standalone comprehensive local gate.
on:
  workflow_call:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:

env:
